notes.b1/j1/B-r1: Spectrum flat shapes with a handle-tagged square and a soft gradient field give an editor-canvas feel; every keyframe ends at its start value so the seam is clean, though the shape collage is a fairly familiar screensaver pattern.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Recreates the Figma five-piece logo in its exact brand colors, which breaks the no-logo-copying rule; the scatter, assemble, explode, reassemble choreography is clear, but the backOut restart from the scatter hold gives a velocity kink at the seam.
notes.b1/j1/B-r2: Its primitives, stripe pattern activation and starburst carry Figma's editor energy without copying the logo, but the starburst rotation runs 0 to 90 degrees and then snaps back at the seam because the shape has no 90-degree symmetry, despite the source comment claiming otherwise.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Staggered overshoot-bezier assembly with a dark blurred glow is the most polished motion here and loops cleanly, but it reproduces the Figma logo with its brand colors, and the pieces fly off-stage mid-loop, leaving the frame nearly empty at 3.6 s.
notes.b1/j2/B-r2: Flat spectrum primitives with a nice striped pattern fill avoid copying the logo, but the scattered generic shapes read as a shape screensaver, and the starburst's rotation seam likely pops because its 12-vertex path is not 45-degree symmetric as the source claims.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: The dark ground with blurred brand-colored glows and staggered overshoot assembly has strong Figma energy and a clean keyframe match at 0 and 100 percent, but it rebuilds the Figma logo mark piece for piece, which the brief forbids.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: The assemble, explode and return sequence loops exactly with a subtle breathing scale, but it is a literal copy of the Figma logo on a plain grey ground, its backOut ease is dead code, and pieces clip at the SVG edge during the explode.
notes.b1/j2/B-r1: Playful brand shapes with a Figma-style selection-handle square, starburst and gradient field capture the brand energy without any logo, with multi-layer choreography, per-keyframe easing that returns every element to its start, a click-to-pause control and a responsive container that holds up on phones.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Dark glow field with a staggered assemble, burst and reassemble that loops cleanly from an invisible seam, but it redraws the Figma logo mark itself, which hurts originality.
notes.b1/j3/B-r2: Flat spectrum shapes on a soft pastel gradient with a slow, exact periodic loop, though the motion is calm and the composition is sparse with a visible letterbox band on desktop.
notes.b1/j3/B-r1: Varied-easing shapes on a gradient field, with white selection-style handles that reference the Figma editor, and a clean seam and responsive card layout.
notes.b1/j3/A-r1: A literal Figma logo assemble-explode on flat gray, with pieces clipped at the viewBox edge mid-loop and a small velocity kink where the backOut segment starts at the seam.
notes.b2/j1/B-r3: Clean periodic sinusoidal drift of Figma-palette flat shapes with a seamless 5 s loop, but it is a generic shape screensaver with no choreography and the blue square and red pill read as filler.
notes.b2/j1/A-r3: Five flat pieces assemble, burst outward and reassemble on a dark glow with eased keyframes and a per-piece stagger, and the last keyframe equals the first so the seam is clean; the assembled cluster edges close to the Figma mark arrangement and the lighter-blend blooms look a little muddy.
notes.b2/j1/B-r4: The selection-handles-on-a-square idea is a nice Figma UI reference, but the starburst's CSS transform overrides its SVG translate so it is pinned to the top-left corner in every frame, which is a visible bug, and the motion is only two simple beats.
notes.b2/j1/A-r4: Staggered overshooting assembly of five pieces on a dark glow is well timed and loops cleanly, but the assembled frame is essentially the Figma logo itself, which goes against the no-logo-copying rule, and the long empty gap near the end of the cycle drags.
notes.b2/j2/B-r4: Pastel gradient with flat circle, square and starburst reads Figma-adjacent and loops cleanly on a 5 s ease-out/hold/ease-in-out cycle, but the starburst's CSS transform overrides its translate, so it sits clipped in the top-left corner in every frame and the composition looks sparse and broken.
notes.b2/j2/A-r4: Staggered canvas pieces scatter, assemble with spin and eased easing, then disperse, with a wrap-based 5 s loop that returns exactly to its start, but the assembled frame reproduces the Figma mark's five-shape arrangement in its exact brand palette, which edges into copying the logo.
notes.b2/j2/A-r3: Clean pastel Figma-palette shapes with a periodic sinusoidal loop that is seamless by construction, but the motion is a generic wandering screensaver with no choreography and the purple circle awkwardly overlaps the red pill.
notes.b2/j2/B-r3: Bright Figma-palette shapes (quarter circle, semicircle, squircle, pill) staggered in and out over soft dark glows with a seamless 5 s wrap, giving the most energetic and brand-like result without copying the logo, though some mid-motion compositions look cramped.
notes.b2/j3/A-r4: Assembles the Figma logo mark piece for piece (half-pill top-left, coral, purple, blue, green circles), which breaks the no-logo rule; otherwise a clean staggered scatter-and-assemble with a seamless opacity-0 seam.
notes.b2/j3/B-r4: Selection-handle idea is a nice Figma nod, but the starburst's CSS transform overrides its SVG translate, so it sits clipped in the top-left corner instead of beside the square.
notes.b2/j3/B-r3: All motion is periodic sine/cosine, so the loop is mathematically exact, but the orbiting, drifting, and bobbing shapes read as a generic shape screensaver with no designed choreography.
notes.b2/j3/A-r3: Uses Figma's exact palette and shape vocabulary (quarter, half, circle, squircle, pill) on a dark glow without copying the logo, with staggered eased assemble, stretch, and scatter that returns exactly to its start.
